label: General contractor — hazardous-materials hauling
summary: The baseline plus the two federal and ISO forms R2 demands of a hazmat hauler: MCS-90 and CA 99 48. Certly does not read either form at launch and says so.

requirements.note: R2 requires the $1,000,000 combined single limit to apply to the vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Statutory workers' compensation, as required by the state the work is performed in.

requirements.label: MCS-90 (federal financial responsibility for hazmat carriers)
requirements.note: R2 requires the MCS-90. It is a federal financial-responsibility endorsement, not a grant of cover to the certificate holder, and it is not printed on an ACORD 25 — ask for the endorsement page.

requirements.label: CA 99 48 (pollution liability — broadened coverage for covered autos)
requirements.note: R2 requires CA 99 48 alongside the MCS-90. It is not printed on an ACORD 25 — ask for the endorsement page.
R1 forbids claims-made general liability without written consent; R5 requires an occurrence basis.
R2, R3 and R5 all require the general aggregate to apply separately to each project.
R1: any deductible or self-insured retention over $25,000 must be disclosed on the certificate and approved.
R2: state fund cover in a monopolistic state does not include employers' liability, so a stop-gap endorsement is required there.
